title: Transport for the Malta trip (13–19 October 2026)
intro: Start with the organizer’s actual attendee location and daily finish time. Route 186 and Route 214 are public-bus candidates between Qawra and Ta’ Qali, not confirmed hotel-to-entrance journeys. Malta Public Transport’s published fares were read directly on 11 October 2026 (single day-route journeys €2.50 in the summer window / €2.00 in winter, €3.00 night and Tallinja Direct, €3.50 on TD1, €19 for 12 journeys, €25 for the 7-day Explore Adult card), and travel cards can be bought at the Buġibba Terminal. Ticket-holder access to the Thunderpick Finals is still unconfirmed; use the date-specific planner for both directions and keep a live-quote taxi fallback, especially for the 17 October evening diversion. Confirmed 11 October 2026: the attendee venue is BLAST Arena Studios Malta, MFCC South Gate National Stadium, ATD 4000 Attard, running 14–18 October with event days listed to 22:00–22:30. That outlasts the last listed bus departure from the Ta’ Qali Stadium area (20:53), so plan a taxi or ride-hailing return, or leave early.

records.notes: Confirmed 11 October 2026 from the official ticketing listing https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/hotspawn-present-the-thunderpick-world-championships-2026-tickets-1988838616841 : venue BLAST Arena Studios Malta, MFCC South Gate National Stadium, ATD 4000 Attard; map coordinates 35.8957343, 14.4168839; Wednesday 14 – Sunday 18 October; 9:30 AM – 10 PM; Wed 14 and Thu 15 check-in 09:30 / games 10:30 to 22:30; Fri 16 check-in 14:00 / games 15:00 to 21:00. Sat 17 and Sun 18 agenda entries were behind a “Show all agenda” control and remain unconfirmed. Organizer window: https://world-championship.thunderpick.io/2026-finals/ . Thunderpick release naming BLAST Studios Malta: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thunderpick-world-championship-2026-returns-to-malta-with-1-million-prize-pool-302850221.html . Field announcement datelined TA’ QALI: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thunderpick-world-championship-2026-reveals-eight-team-field-for-1-million-malta-finals-302880720.html . Enter the address or the coordinates in https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ for each event date rather than relying on a route name.

records.name: Qawra ↔ Ta’ Qali Stadium — Route 186 (direct bus to the event area)
records.address: Operator stop sequence: Qawra 952 → Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227 (Rabat-bound); Stadium 2194 → Buġibba (return). Verify stop sides, safe walks and the onward hotel connection in the dated planner.
records.hours: Operator timetable read 11 October 2026: Il-Qawra stops served roughly 06:08–21:39 and Ta’ Qali Stadium stop 6227 roughly 06:39–22:08, on a repeating 30-minute pattern. Journey Qawra 952 → Stadium 6227 is about 30 minutes in the published grid. The extracted page carries several timetable variants without reliable day-type context, so treat these as static-grid spans rather than trip-day guarantees and confirm the date-specific departure in the operator’s planner.
records.description: Route 186 runs between Rabat and Buġibba and is the only route in the operator’s tables that links Qawra’s seafront stops directly to the Ta’ Qali stadium stop. Read on 11 October 2026, the published stop grids give Il-Qawra Arznell (950) 06:08–21:38, Il-Qawra Luzzu (951) 06:08–21:38 and Qawra (952) 06:09–21:39, and Ta’ Qali Stadium (6227) 06:39–22:08, all on a 30-minute repeating pattern; the difference between Qawra 952 and Stadium 6227 in the same run is about 30 minutes. For the return, board the opposite-side Stadium stop (2194) toward Buġibba, which is not a Qawra seafront stop — plan a separate connection to the hotel. These are published static departure grids for the current timetable, not a saved date-specific journey, and the walk from stop 6227 or 2194 to the actual MFCC/BLAST gate has not been measured.
records.notes: Operator route page with the stop-by-stop grids, read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . Stops confirmed in that page’s lists: Il-Qawra Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952, Ta’ Qali Gibjun 6118, Venture 6226, Stadium 6227 and Villagg 6228; Rabat 4 (2567) is the other terminus. The same page shows stops 6227/6228/2191 also served by Routes 56 and 202, and the Stadium 6227 stop is also listed for the Ta’ Qali Park & Ride shuttles 403, 404 and 405 — useful alternates to compare in the planner. Route 214 lists Qawra and Qali-area stops as a second option: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/214/ . For the Saturday 17 October evening diversion see the separate diversion record. Date-specific planner (not run here): https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . The operator’s public notice of the 17 October diversion is at https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Second-session caveats (11 October 2026): the static page shows multiple time variants and earlier tighter bounds were withdrawn rather than presented as trip-day times; the date-specific planner is https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . Return stop 2194 was independently re-read on 11 October; outbound 6227 and return 2194 are different direction stops, so no single clock range is asserted. Route 186 is a day route, so a single journey costs the day-route price and is covered by the 7-day Explore Adult card; the closest listed sales office to Qawra is the Buġibba Terminal: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ .
records.price range: Single day-route fare is €2.00 winter / €2.50 summer as published; the operator’s stated winter effective range (19 October 2025 – 13 June 2026) does not cover the trip window, so confirm on board or use a travel card.

records.name: Route 186 diversion — every Friday and Saturday evening, starting 17 October
records.address: Route 186 toward Buġibba; affected stops listed by MPT are Gholja 2 through Targa
records.hours: Weekly on Friday and Saturday, 19:00–00:00, starting 17 October 2026 and ending 18 October 2026 at approximately 00:00
records.description: Malta Public Transport’s Route 186 page carries a detour notice effective weekly on Fridays and Saturdays from 19:00 to 00:00, starting 17 October and ending 18 October at approximately 00:00, and states that toward Buġibba the stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served. Because 17 October is a Playoffs day and the notice names only those intermediate stops, the notice does not by itself say whether a Ta’ Qali Stadium departure or a Qawra-ward connection is cancelled. The same page carries a separate, longer-running weekly Friday/Saturday 20:00–00:00 detour ending 21 April with the same affected-stop wording, so the operator is publishing overlapping notices and the live planner should be treated as authoritative on the day.
records.notes: Read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ under “Latest Service Updates”: a detour weekly on Friday and Saturday 19:00–00:00 starting 17 October, ending 18 October at about 00:00, “Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served”; and a second notice weekly on Friday and Saturday 20:00–00:00 ending 21 April with identical affected-stop wording. The same page also lists a stop closure at Saqqajja (ID 4627) on Routes 109, 109A, 181, 182, 186, 201, 202, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56 and N52, ends 1 January approximately 04:00, and Tuesday 13 October 09:30–17:30 construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. All-service-updates page: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Do not infer a cancelled or extra TWC service from these notices. The notice specifies affected stops rather than a total cancellation of Route 186, and it does not itself confirm whether a particular post-event bus will serve the required Qawra stop. Also listed on the operator’s service-updates page on 11 October 2026: Tuesday 13 October (09:30–17:30) construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. Recheck the operator’s updates and planner on the day. Independently re-read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . The live notice reads: “Buses on Route 186 will be on detour. Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served.” Ambiguity to note: 17 October 2026 is a Saturday and the explicit end time is 18 October at approximately 12:00 AM (that is, midnight ending Saturday 17 October), yet the same sentence says the detour runs “weekly on Friday, Saturday”. Whether it also applies on Friday 16 October is therefore not clear from the text and must be checked with the operator or the planner. The notice also describes the Buġibba-bound direction only; it does not say whether the Ta’ Qali Stadium stops used by this trip are affected.
records.price range: Normal route fare; no separate event fare published

records.name: Malta Airport ↔ Qawra by Airport Direct TD1 (Il-Qawra stop Arznell 950)
records.area: Malta International Airport ↔ Qawra / Buġibba / north Malta
records.address: Airport bus terminal (Airport 1 stop 2550 outbound; Airport 3 stop 2552 return) ↔ Il-Qawra stop Arznell (ID 950) and Buġibba stops Sajf (947), Bugibba Bay 8 (2339), and Wileg (955). Confirm the stop nearest the hotel entrance in the planner.
records.hours: MPT’s Route TD1 timetable (read 11 Oct 2026) lists hourly departures from Airport 1 (stop 2550) on the hour from 05:00 to 00:00, reaching Il-Qawra stop Arznell (950) at 05:42–00:35; return departures toward Airport 3 (stop 2552) serve Il-Qawra stop Arznell (950) hourly at 05:28–23:26 on weekdays and 05:27–23:27 on weekends.
records.description: This is the most straightforward published public-bus option from Malta International Airport toward Qawra: Airport Direct TD1 runs from the airport toward Ċirkewwa via Buġibba and the Qawra area, and its operator timetable confirms service at Il-Qawra stop Arznell (ID 950) in both directions. The airport terminal is signposted from arrivals. Buses have luggage space; no advance booking is required. The precise walk from stop Arznell 950 to AX ODYCY was not independently measured.
records.notes: Route stop and times: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/TD1/. MPT also lists TD5 Airport Direct toward Rabat/Buġibba hourly at €3; its Qawra suitability was not established here. Operator information and fares: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/. Independently re-read 11 October (chunks 7–9): both the Airport 1 outbound sequence (05:42–00:35 at Arznell 950) and the Ċirkewwa-to-Airport 3 return sequence (05:28–23:26 weekday / 05:27–23:27 weekend at Arznell 950) serve Il-Qawra stop Arznell 950. This supports route-level Qawra service in both directions, while the hotel walk and flight-specific departure still require a journey-planner check. Fare context re-verified 11 October 2026 against the operator’s own table, which lists Tallinja Direct routes at €3.00 and TD1 at €3.50: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . The same page states that the 7-day Explore Adult card excludes tallinja Direct routes, while the 12 Single Day Journeys card may be used on the Airport Direct service at a cost of two journeys per trip.
records.price range: €3.50 per passenger on TD1 without an eligible unlimited travel card; cash or contactless onboard

records.name: Bus fares, travel cards and where to buy them (operator table, 11 October 2026)
records.address: Tickets may be purchased onboard by cash or contactless; sales points and machines are listed by MPT
records.hours: Tickets are valid for two hours with free transfers inside that window. Missed-ticket penalty: €50. Explore Child 7-day is €7.00 (ages 4–10). Cards and singles are sold at the airport, the Valletta and Buġibba terminals and Sliema Ferries, and the page does not print the 2026/27 winter changeover date.
records.description: The operator’s fare page, read 11 October 2026, publishes a single ticket table and a separate card table. Singles bought from the driver with cash, a contactless bank card or a phone are €2.00 (winter) or €2.50 (summer) on day routes and are valid for two hours with free transfers. The 12 Single Day Journeys card costs €19.00 and is shareable between travellers; the Explore Flex card costs €21.00 for four days or €27.00 for seven days and its offer grid explicitly includes Day Routes, Night Routes, Airport Direct and Special Services; the separate Explore Adult 7-day card at €25.00 explicitly excludes tallinja Direct Routes. A €50 penalty applies to travellers who cannot show a valid ticket, and cards must be validated on boarding. The page states the winter €2.00 single-fare period as running from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026, which does not resolve which single fare applies during 13–19 October 2026.
records.notes: Fare page read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . Card-sales locations and machines: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . TD1 Airport Direct detail: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/other-services/airport-direct/ . Worked comparison for a seven-day trip that includes airport days and daily event travel: Explore Flex 7-day €27.00 already includes Airport Direct, which would otherwise cost TD1 singles at €3.50 each way (€7.00 return); Explore Adult 7-day €25.00 plus two TD1 singles is about €32.00, and a 12-journey €19.00 card would be partly consumed by the two extra Airport Direct journeys. That comparison is arithmetic on published prices, not a quote, and assumes the traveller actually needs Airport Direct and daily buses. The page also sells Explore Flex bundle upgrades that add a Gozo Highspeed return (€42.00 for 7 days) or a harbour cruise (€42.00 for 7 days). Confirm activation, expiry and inclusions at a sales office before buying. Sales offices and ticket machines: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . The page states that the €2.00 winter fare applied from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026 and lists a separate summer day-route fare of €2.50, but it does not print the 2026/27 winter start date, so the exact seasonal boundary for this trip stays open. Recheck the day before travel, because seasonal prices and card inclusions change.
records.price range: On-board/contactless single: €2.00 winter day route, €2.50 summer day route; night route €3.00; Special Service €3.00; tallinja Direct €3.00; TD1 €3.50. Cards: 12 Single Day Journeys €19.00 (shareable); Explore Flex 4-day €21.00 and 7-day €27.00 (both include Day, Night, Airport Direct and Special Services); Explore Adult 7-day €25.00 (excludes tallinja Direct Routes); Explore Child 7-day €7.00.

records.name: Event-day plan A — public bus Qawra → Ta’ Qali Stadium (Route 186)
records.address: Board at Qawra (952) / Luzzu (951) / Il-Qawra Arznell (950); alight at Ta’ Qali Stadium (6227)
records.hours: Outbound boards roughly 06:09–21:39 from Qawra 952, arriving Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227 about 30 minutes later, every 30 minutes. Return boards the opposite-side Stadium stop 2194 toward Buġibba; the operator’s grid shows a last listed 20:53 departure with a Buġibba Bay 1 arrival at 21:27.
records.price range: €2.50 summer / €2.00 winter single per person per direction if the seasonal boundary falls where expected; €19.00 for 12 shareable journeys; €27.00 for a 7-day Explore Flex card that also covers Airport Direct, Night Routes and Special Services.
records.description: Planning sequence for each event day. 1) Confirm on the organizer’s channels what time the doors actually open and close, because no TWC spectator schedule is published and a late playoff finish is the biggest risk. 2) Buy or top up a card that covers Day Routes — the €27.00 Explore Flex 7-day card is the only published card whose own offer grid explicitly includes Airport Direct, Night Routes and Special Services — or pay €2.50 per single on board if the summer fare still applies. 3) Ask the hotel front desk which Qawra stop side is correct and how long the walk is; Qawra 952, Luzzu 951 and Il-Qawra Arznell 950 are all listed on Route 186 within a few minutes of each other. 4) Board toward Rabat and alight at Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227. 5) For the return, cross to Stadium 2194 and board toward Buġibba, then connect onward to the hotel by a second bus or a short taxi hop, because that direction does not serve the Qawra seafront. 6) If the finish is after about 20:53, take a taxi or ride-hailing car instead — no night route serving Ta’ Qali or Ħ’Attard was found, and night routes were verified only from Buġibba (N212) and Valletta (N13).
records.notes: This is a planning sequence assembled from the operator’s own published grids and notices, not a verified door-to-door journey. Underlying sources: Route 186 stop grids https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ (read 11 October 2026); fares and card inclusions https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ ; service notices https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ ; night-route announcement https://www.publictransport.com.mt/new-night-routes/ ; date-specific planner https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . Unverified pieces: the walk from each Qawra stop to AX ODYCY, the walk from Stadium 6227/2194 to the actual MFCC/BLAST gate, the correct side of the road at each stop, and whether Route 186 runs to plan on the specific dates. The operator’s own Route 186 page also lists a Friday/Saturday evening diversion starting 17 October. Re-run the planner on the day and keep a live Bolt, eCabs, Uber or Malta Taxi quote as the fallback: https://bolt.eu/en/cities/malta/ , https://ecabs.com.mt/ , https://www.uber.com/global/en/r/cities/valletta-valletta-mt/ , https://www.maltataxi.mt/ . Session note: this plan and the records it cites were assembled across both 11 October verification sessions; where the two sessions differ, the more cautious figure is kept (static timetable spans are labelled as such, and the operator’s date-specific planner remains authoritative).

records.name: Which single-journey fare applies during 13–19 October 2026
records.address: Not applicable — fare rules
records.hours: Malta Public Transport’s fare page read 11 October 2026 lists day-route singles at €2.50 (summer) and €2.00 (winter) and states that the €2.00 winter fare applied from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026. It does not print the start date of the 2026/27 winter period. Applied to this trip: 13–18 October 2026 falls in the summer window (€2.50) and 19 October 2026 — the departure day — falls on the winter rate (€2.00). Because the page prints no explicit summer 2026 range, this is an inference from the published winter boundary and is kept at “partially verified”; confirm in the tallinja app on arrival.
records.description: The trip runs 13–19 October 2026. On the operator’s own pattern the cheaper winter single begins after 19 October, so the higher summer single price is the planning figure to budget for this trip; the operator’s page does not state the 2026/27 changeover date, so this remains a planning inference, not a published trip-week fare. Budget either way with the day-route single (€2.50), or buy a travel card, which removes the uncertainty for a multi-day stay.
records.notes: Evidence: the official fare table and the sentence “With effect from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026, the winter fare of €2.00 … applies”: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . The trip window (13–19 October) sits inside a period the operator prices as summer on its own published table, but no 2026/27 winter start date is printed, and third-party guides that assert specific changeover dates are not operator sources and were not adopted. Resolve by rechecking the operator page or the tallinja app immediately before travel.
records.price range: Planning figure €2.50 per single day-route journey during the trip; €2.00 winter rate expected to resume after 19 October 2026 (not published on the checked page) Trip-specific reading: €2.50 per single day-route journey on 13–18 October 2026 and €2.00 on 19 October 2026 (inference, not a quoted range).

records.name: Ride-hailing in Malta — Bolt, eCabs and the conflicting Uber status
records.area: Malta (provider pages and two conflicting 2026 guides); coverage in Qawra and at the Ta’ Qali venue not verified
records.address: Pickup/drop-off set in the Uber app
records.hours: App-based, on demand; provider pages describe 24/7 requesting but no trip-time availability or waiting time was verified.
records.price range: Live in-app quotes only: Uber’s own page quotes about €20 for an average 19-minute UberX trip from MLA; no Qawra–Ta’ Qali or event-night price verified, and third-party airport-to-Buġibba estimates (roughly €25–€35) are guide figures, not quotes
records.description: Two ride-hailing providers are documented as operating in Malta: Bolt, described in Maltese national media as the leading ride-hailing platform on the islands and offering English-language service through its Malta pages, and eCabs, a long-standing Maltese operator with pre-booking. Uber’s position is contradictory in the sources checked on 11 October 2026: Uber publishes a Malta airport page that mentions UberX rides with an average €20 fare for roughly 19-minute trips from MLA, while two 2026 third-party guides state that Uber does not operate in Malta. Treat Bolt and eCabs as the reliable options, confirm Uber in the app on arrival, and never accept an unlicensed driver approaching inside the terminal.
records.notes: Uber’s Malta airport page read 11 October 2026: https://www.uber.com/global/en/r/airports/mla/taxi/ (it says taxis are not available for MLA rides and points riders to UberX, quoting an average €20 for a 19-minute trip). Conflicting third-party guides also read 11 October 2026: https://www.malta-spirit.com/guides/taxis-bolt-and-ride-share-malta/ and https://hubpymalta.com/what-to-do/malta-airport-guide.html (both say Uber does not operate in Malta). Bolt’s presence in Malta is reported by Times of Malta: https://timesofmalta.com/article/bolt-becomes-first-ridehailing-app-available-maltese.1117399 , with provider pages at https://bolt.eu/en/cities/malta/ and https://bolt.eu/en/airports/mla/ . eCabs: https://ecabs.com.mt/ . No Qawra–Ta’ Qali quote, event-night supply, pickup point or waiting time was verified for any provider; compare live quotes and keep the bus as the priced fallback.

records.name: Transport mode comparison — convenience, price, value & feasibility
records.area: Malta-wide (airport, Qawra, Ta’ Qali and island connections)
records.address: Not applicable — mode-by-mode comparison across published operator services
records.hours: Depends on mode and date. Route 186 and TD1 are published options; exact trip-date routing, safe walks, service changes and event access require the live operator planner and confirmed destination.
records.price range: Verified operator prices for budgeting: day-route single €2.50 summer / €2.00 winter (2-hour transfers); night, Special Services and Tallinja Direct €3.00; TD1 €3.50; 12 Single Day Journeys €19; Explore Adult 7-day €25; Explore Child €7; Explore Flex 4-day €21 / 7-day €27; €50 fine without a valid ticket. Taxi/ride-hailing and car hire need live quotes; ferry fares depend on route.
records.description: Convenience, price, value and feasibility compared for the Qawra base: public buses are the only fully publicly priced mode, and on 11 October 2026 the operator’s own fare table, card terms and sales points were read directly so the planner can use exact figures instead of inferred ones. Route 186 connects Qawra to Ta’ Qali with a return via Buġibba; taxis and ride-hailing are door-to-door but unquoted; a rental car only makes sense if the traveler accepts left-side driving, insurance excess and unverified venue parking. The unresolved variables are the confirmed TWC access/entrance, the daily finish time and the 17 October evening diversion. Route 186 specifics: the operator’s static grid lists Qawra 952 at 06:09–21:39 and Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227 at 06:39–22:08 on a repeating 30-minute pattern, putting the stadium roughly 30 minutes from the Qawra seafront stop, with the return boarding opposite-side Stadium 2194 toward Buġibba — not Qawra seafront — and the operator publishing overlapping Friday/Saturday evening diversions from 17 October.
records.notes: Comparison uses operator and provider sources in this dataset: MPT planner https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ ; Route 186 https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ ; Route 214 https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/214/ ; Airport Direct https://www.publictransport.com.mt/other-services/airport-direct/ and TD1 timetable https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/TD1/ ; fares https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ ; service updates https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ ; night routes https://www.publictransport.com.mt/new-night-routes/ ; Bolt https://bolt.eu/en/cities/malta/ ; eCabs https://ecabs.com.mt/ ; Uber https://www.uber.com/global/en/r/cities/valletta-valletta-mt/ ; Malta Taxi https://www.maltataxi.mt/ ; airport rental https://maltairport.com/renting-a-car/ ; Valletta Ferry Services https://www.vallettaferryservices.com/ ; Gozo Channel https://www.gozochannel.com/ferry/fares/passenger/ ; Gozo Highspeed https://gozohighspeed.com/pages/fares . TD1 Arznell 950 departure/direction and hotel walking distance remain trip-planner checks. No taxi/rental quote, physical route test, exact TWC location, or door-to-door event journey was established. October single-fare validity remains open. Repriced 11 October 2026 from the operator’s published table and card terms: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . The same page confirms the two-hour transfer window, the excluded tallinja Direct routes from the 7-day Explore card, and the €50 fine for travelling without a valid ticket.

records.name: TWC 2026 — attendee access confirmed; entrance gate and two agenda days still unpublished
records.area: BLAST Arena Studios / MFCC, Ta’ Qali, Ħ’Attard
records.address: Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre, Ta’ Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard, Malta
records.hours: Ticketing listing (read 11 October 2026): Wednesday 14 – Sunday 18 October 2026, 9:30 AM – 10 PM. Check-in 09:30 / games 10:30 (to 22:30) on 14 and 15 October; check-in 14:00 / games 15:00 (to 21:00) on 16 October. The 17 and 18 October entries sit behind a “Show all agenda” control and are not published.
records.price range: Free admission — the listing shows a free “Reserve a spot” action and no paid tier. This supersedes the €10.00 studio-audience precedent from a separate BLAST-run event at the same studio, which does not apply to these Finals.
records.description: Attendance is confirmed: the event’s own ticketing listing publishes the venue, the 14–18 October dates, day-by-day check-in and game times for three of the five days, an 18+ in-person audience and free tickets. Two things are still unknown and matter for transport — the attendee gate inside the MFCC site, and the Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October agenda. The published finish times (21:00–22:30) are all later than the last listed bus departure from the Ta’ Qali Stadium area (20:53), so a late CS2 finish is the main risk to any bus-based return. Thunderpick also streams all matches live on its Twitch, Kick and YouTube channels.
records.notes: Superseded in part on 11 October 2026. This record previously reported that no public ticket sale, spectator policy, attendee entrance or daily door time had been found, and that in-person attendance should be treated as unconfirmed. The event’s official ticketing listing https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/hotspawn-present-the-thunderpick-world-championships-2026-tickets-1988838616841 now confirms the venue (BLAST Arena Studios Malta, MFCC South Gate National Stadium, ATD 4000 Attard; coordinates 35.8957343, 14.4168839), the dates, the 18+ in-person audience, free “Reserve a spot” ticketing and the 14/15/16 October agenda. Free ticketing is also reported by HLTV: https://www.hltv.org/news/45615/thunderpick-world-championship-talent-revealed . The organizer’s own page still lists only phase windows and “Stay tuned for the latest details on match schedules, teams, and results”: https://world-championship.thunderpick.io/2026-finals/ . Still open, and the reason this record stays “partially verified”: the attendee gate/entrance inside the MFCC site, the Sat 17 and Sun 18 agenda entries, per-day ticket validity and scanning, venue parking, and on-site catering — all of which sit behind interactive controls on the listing or are organizer questions. The BLAST guest guide for a separate earlier event at the same studio still must not be copied onto these dates for bag policy or gate directions. See docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md for the resolution steps.

records.name: The event outlasts the bus — plan a taxi or ride-hailing return
records.address: BLAST Arena Studios Malta, MFCC South Gate National Stadium, ATD 4000 Attard, Malta — the address printed on the official ticketing page for this event. The listing also publishes map coordinates 35.8957343, 14.4168839. The attendee gate inside the site is not specified.
records.hours: Conflict to plan around. The ticketing listing runs the event to 10:00–10:30 PM on the three days whose agenda is visible (14, 15 and 16 October). The last listed Route 186 departure from the Ta’ Qali Stadium area is 20:53, with a listed Buġibba Bay 1 arrival of 21:27, and the normal return runs via St Paul’s Bay/Buġibba rather than the Qawra seafront. Staying to the end of an event day therefore means no bus return.
records.price range: Bus option €2.50 per single journey (summer table); the late return needs a live taxi or ride-hailing quote, which has not been obtained.
records.description: This is the single most important transport finding for the trip. On 14, 15 and 16 October the event is listed until 22:00–22:30, which is later than the last published Route 186 departure from the Ta’ Qali Stadium area. Options: leave before the last bus, or book a taxi/ride-hailing return for the end of the night. On Saturday 17 October the Route 186 evening detour adds a further complication toward Buġibba. MPT’s night routes do not serve the event area, so get a live quote in Bolt, eCabs, Uber or Malta Taxi before you travel out.
records.notes: Derived by comparing two dated operator sources read on 11 October 2026. Event end time: the official ticketing listing https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/hotspawn-present-the-thunderpick-world-championships-2026-tickets-1988838616841 shows 09:30–22:30 on Wed 14 and Thu 15 October and 14:00–21:00 on Fri 16 October, under an overall header of 9:30 AM – 10 PM for 14–18 October. Bus end of service: the Route 186 record in this dataset, from https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ , lists a last Stadium departure of 20:53 and a Buġibba Bay 1 arrival of 21:27. Night routes: MPT’s own announcement https://www.publictransport.com.mt/new-night-routes/ covers Buġibba (N212) and Valletta (N13) and does not list Ta’ Qali or Attard, so it is not a substitute for the event return. The Saturday 17 October evening is additionally affected by the Route 186 detour published on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . What is NOT verified: a live taxi or ride-hailing fare for this journey, whether the organizer adds event shuttles, the Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 event finish times, and the walking route between the MFCC gate and the nearest stop. Run each date through https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ and keep a live quote as the fallback.
